title: MZ Building 'Twilight In Arcania': A Developer's Journal

posts.author: punitdh89
posts.body:
Hello everyone!
I'm thrilled to begin this journey with all of you. My name is Punit, and I'm a software engineer specializing in JavaScript. Let me share a bit about myself and the exciting project I'm working on.
About Me:
Profession:
Software Engineer, primarily focused on JavaScript.
Passion for Games:
I've always been passionate about games, both playing and creating them. I'm a huge fan of all kinds of RPGs—JRPGs, western RPGs, etc. My current favorite games are
Undertale
,
Deltarune
,
To The Moon
(an RPG Maker classic), and the
Final Fantasy
series.
Game Development Journey:
I've been dabbling in game development since 2003.
Challenges:
Despite my long-standing passion, I’ve never finished a game till now because I struggled to find an engine that truly suited my needs. I mostly used GameMaker Studio before this but found it a bit tedious due to having to build everything from scratch (anyone who has used GMS/GMS2 will know what I'm talking about).
Asset Creation:
Asset creation has always been a stumbling block for me, often causing me to stall in my projects.
RPG Maker MZ:
Discovering RPG Maker MZ and its fantastic RTP and JavaScript features has been a game-changer. I finally feel right at home, equipped with the tools I need to bring my vision to life.
Comment on RTP:
Even though the RTP provided by RPG Maker MZ is fantastic, I take every step necessary to customize it—be it by adding lighting, shadows, parallax mapping, and/or any assortment of available plugins.
About the Game:
I'm excited to share that I'm working on a game called "Twilight in Arcania." Here's a brief overview of what the game is about:
Twilight in Arcania
is a fantasy RPG set in a richly detailed world filled with magic, mystery, and dark secrets. The story follows Ethan, a young protagonist who, guided by mysterious dreams of his late father, embarks on a quest to uncover the truth behind a legendary artifact known as a
Terribly-Rusted Sword
. Along the way, he will encounter memorable characters, face difficult moral choices, and navigate treacherous environments.
Key Features:
Engaging Story:
A compelling narrative that explores themes of betrayal, redemption, and the characters' personal struggles.
Rich Characters:
Every character Ethan meets has a unique backstory and meaningful development arcs.
Morally Gray Choices:
Players will face tough decisions that have significant impacts on the story and characters.
Light And Dark Moments:
The game will balance intensely dark and emotional moments with comic relief and humor, so that it doesn't get too overwhelming for some players.
Challenging Puzzles:
Players will need to solve intricate puzzles and make strategic decisions to progress.
Meaningful Encounters:
Instead of random encounters, each enemy you face has significance, making every battle a meaningful part of the story.
Atmospheric World:
A beautifully crafted world brought to life with detailed art and an evocative soundtrack.
Usage of AI:
I have used AI to generate a few of the elements in the game, such as the title screen and also to enhance some of the battler sprites.
I have studied the art of game development closely for over 10 years and feel confident enough to finish this project. I have also completed the first two "quests" of the game and I am close to finishing a demo, which I am excited to share with you all soon.
Without giving away too many spoilers, I've taken steps to make
Twilight in Arcania
a game that pulls players into a deep, immersive experience.
Stay tuned in this thread, because I do plan to share my progress, challenges, and insights throughout the development process. Excited to be on this journey, and I look forward to any feedback and support.
Thank you for being part of this adventure.

Update - September 2024
Hello everyone,
I'm thrilled to share some updates on the development of
Twilight in Arcania
, and also give a bit more background on what I've been working on over the past few months.
Background:
I've been developing
Twilight in Arcania
using RPG Maker MZ, where I’m focusing on creating a compelling narrative with meaningful gameplay mechanics. I’ve always loved rich, story-driven RPGs like
Undertale
,
Final Fantasy
, and
To The Moon
, and I’m channeling that inspiration into this project.
Development has been progressing smoothly, and I’ve been working on new mechanics and lore to make the world of Arcania even more immersive.
My goal has been to craft an atmospheric world filled with moral dilemmas, emotionally deep characters, and gameplay that feels equally rewarding and challenging. Asset creation has been one of the trickier parts of the journey, but the flexible nature of RPG Maker MZ and with the help of VisuStellaMZ plugins, combined with custom lighting, shadows, parallax mapping, and plugins, has made the process enjoyable and fulfilling.
Recent Progress:
New Town with Lore:
I've added a new village to the game, known for its heritage in dragon breeding. In this town, there is a dragon who once roamed the wilds under a powerful name but has since been tamed by the villagers and renamed to something more playful. Trying to give the village a unique and interesting atmosphere.
Visual Overhaul with Parallax Mapping:
Over the past few weeks, I’ve been heavily focused on parallax mapping (
see screenshots below
) for both indoor and outdoor areas, experimenting with lighting effects and overlays to give the game a moody and immersive feel. Even in outdoor settings like forests, the use of semi-transparent overlays with subtle light rays has created a dark, atmospheric environment that aligns with the game’s tone.
Boss Fights and Combat Mechanics:
I’ve been hard at work making boss battles more dynamic and intense. Instead of relying on random moves, key battles now follow a scripted turn-by-turn mechanic that adds strategy and tension. One boss, a former royal mage, can summon allies and even transform mid-battle, adding layers of challenge that I believe will keep players on their toes.
Expanding the Lore and Mythology:
A significant portion of the game's story revolves around ancient gods and mythical forces. In one of the game’s central locations, players will encounter powerful beings engaged in a centuries-old family feud. These divine characters play a crucial role in shaping the world and the events of the story. The introduction of these mythological elements is designed to add emotional depth to the plot.
Playtesting & Feedback:
I’ve spent a lot of time refining the combat, lighting, and overall feel of the environments. The game feels darker and more immersive, but I’m always tweaking things based on playtesting to ensure every scene feels impactful. I’ve also been fine-tuning combat to make sure it stays engaging and challenging.
What’s Next?
I’m working towards finishing a demo of the game soon and can’t wait to share it with the community. It’s been a long journey, but it's bringing me closer to realizing the vision I have for
Twilight in Arcania
.
Thank you to everyone for your support and feedback along the way. Stay tuned for more updates, and feel free to ask questions or offer any insights!
Best,
Punit

Dev Log Update - June 2025
Hey everyone,
It's been over 8 months since my last update, but I haven't been slacking off. I did take a 4 month break for personal reasons, but now I'm back on track, and I've been laser-focused on building what feels like my magnum opus. "Twilight in Arcania" has grown into something much bigger and more meaningful than when I first started. I've overhauled the core systems, tightened the story, and polished countless little things to bring the world to life.
Here's a look at what I've been doing (sorry, but no demo yet):
Narrative Progress
Without giving away spoilers, I can say this: the story has evolved. Twilight in Arcania isn't just a fantasy tale anymore. It's about trauma, memory, betrayal, and resilience. Ethan's journey is no longer just about exploring the world; it's about unravelling its lies, confronting divine indifference, and choosing who he wants to become in the middle of it all. Many of the emotional story beats are fully written and implemented, and the pacing has been reworked to make sure each moment hits the way it should.
The companion characters have become more fleshed out. Relationships matter in this game, and the bonds Ethan forms will carry emotional weight. There are laugh-out-loud scenes, gut-punch moments, and dark revelations that (I hope) will stick with players long after they close the game.
Custom Plugins & Systems
I've written an absurd number of custom systems, many of which could easily be standalone premium plugins. Here's a quick overview:
Loot Manager
: Randomized and deterministic loot tables (weighted, rarity-based, etc.) with consistency. Uses PRNG for reproducible outcomes.
Stagger System (WIP):
Enemies build up a stagger bar from attacks. When full, they enter a vulnerable state where they can be hit with massive damage.
Auto Face Manager (WIP):
Automatically changes actor faces in dialog depending on their current class and emotion. Changing clothes updates the displayed face accordingly.
CommonUtils.js:
My main plugin powering a ton of stuff, including:
Directional enemy selection in battle
(available for download as a free plugin)
Controller right-stick support for menu navigation
Improved number input UI (I hated the default RPG Maker number input)
JS evaluation in message boxes
Event exit resets, map exit common events, and dynamic BGM switching
Quest/objective proximity system with sophisticated pathfinding that always points you to your quest objective / marker
Dialog tables for random/NPC interactions
Plugin commands for streamlined loot, battle, and event logic
Autosave protection on New Game
Advanced Shop System:
Item quantity limits
Merchant gold
Restocking commands
I have plans to make this a
public plugin release
.
Visitable Choices:
Greys out visited dialogue options, Witcher-style.
This is
available for download
as a free plugin.
Non-Plugin Features
Even outside of plugins, I've built some wild systems using just events and clever logic:
Book System:
Readable books/notes with flipping pages (without using the 'Show Picture' command a thousand times
)
Contextual Weather & Time:
Applies tint and weather based on Weather="Rain" or TimeOfDay="Night" using map tagging
Object-Oriented Event Templates
: Almost all events in the game inherit from "parent" events, avoiding copy-pasta and duplicated logic.
Contextual Compass Icons
: Party members can detect treasure, hidden items, or double harvest yield from plants.
What's Next?
I'm in the middle of preparing a demo. Most major scenes and systems are now in place. A few are still being polished, but the game loop is there. From the slow-burn opening in Arcania to the chaos that follows, I'm happy with where it's going.
The game has reached the point where I can finally say: this is the game I would want to play. And that's all I ever really cared about.
Thank you. If you've got feedback, questions or want to try an early build when it's ready, let me know. I'll be dropping screenshots and footage soon.
LATEST:
I recently created a World Map scene that I'd like to share.
Spoiler:
World Map Scene Video
Yes, still using some RTP assets for now, but that's because I've been very busy working on a lot of other systems under the hood. Some of them have been built completely from scratch and optimized for best performance and coding practices (I am a software engineer after all). Post-MVP I plan to go harder on the visuals.
